claims.text: Cyclobenzaprine: usually 5 mg three times a day; by response, may increase to 10 mg three times a day. Use beyond 2 or 3 weeks is not recommended.
claims.quote: For most patients, the recommended dose of cyclobenzaprine hydrochloride tablets is 5 mg three times a day. Based on individual patient response, the dose may be increased to 10 mg three times a day. Use of cyclobenzaprine hydrochloride tablets for periods longer than 2 or 3 weeks is not recommended

claims.text: CI: an MAOI now or within 14 days of stopping one (hyperpyretic crisis, seizures and deaths have occurred).
claims.quote: Concomitant use of monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors or within 14 days after their discontinuation. Hyperpyretic crisis seizures and deaths have occurred in patients receiving cyclobenzaprine (or structurally similar tricyclic antidepressants) concomitantly with MAO inhibitor drugs.

claims.text: CI: acute recovery phase of MI; arrhythmias, heart block or conduction disturbances, or HF.
claims.quote: Acute recovery phase of myocardial infarction, and patients with arrhythmias, heart block or conduction disturbances, or congestive heart failure.

claims.text: Potentially life-threatening serotonin syndrome has been reported with SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, tramadol, bupropion, meperidine, verapamil or MAOIs.
claims.quote: The development of a potentially life-threatening serotonin syndrome has been reported with cyclobenzaprine hydrochloride when used in combination with other drugs, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), tramadol, bupropion, meperidine, verapamil, or (MAO) inhibitors.

claims.text: May enhance the effects of alcohol, barbiturates and other CNS depressants.
claims.quote: Cyclobenzaprine may enhance the effects of alcohol, barbiturates, and other CNS depressants.
